title: Not that ..., but ...
titleEn: Using Not that ..., but ... to correct a possible misunderstanding

omissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules are faithful editorial translations.

example: Not that the idea is bad, but it needs more careful planning.
exampleZh: 並不是說這個想法不好，而是它需要更周詳的規劃。

examples.en: Not that the idea is bad, but it needs more careful planning.
examples.zh: 並不是說這個想法不好，而是它需要更周詳的規劃。
examples.highlight: Not that the idea is bad, but it needs more careful planning.

rules.zh: 在 Not that 後面通常要使用包含主語和動詞的完整子句。
rules.en: Use a complete clause after Not that A clause normally contains a subject and a verb. Not that the restaurant is expensive, but it is too far away. Not that the expensive restaurant, but it is too far away.
examples: Not that the restaurant is expensive, but it is too far away.
Not that the expensive restaurant, but it is too far away.

rules.zh: （並不是說我不喜歡這份工作，而是我需要更有彈性的時間安排。）
rules.en: The second part gives the real point The information after but should explain what the speaker actually thinks, means or wants to emphasise. Not that I dislike the job, but I need a more flexible schedule.
examples: Not that I dislike the job, but I need a more flexible schedule.

rules.zh: 這句並非表示成本完全不重要，而是表示安全才是更重要的考慮。
rules.en: Not that does not always mean that the first idea is completely false It often means: that is not the main point; that is not the real reason; that is not what I am trying to say. Not that the cost is unimportant, but safety should come first. The speaker is not saying that cost is completely unimportant. The speaker is saying that safety is the more important consideration.
examples: that is not the main point;
that is not the real reason;
that is not what I am trying to say.
Not that the cost is unimportant, but safety should come first.

rules.zh: 本課集中練習較簡潔的 Not that ..., but ... 形式。
rules.en: It is a shortened form of It is not that... The following two forms have similar meanings: It is not that the plan is impossible, but it requires more time. Not that the plan is impossible, but it requires more time.
examples: It is a shortened form of It is not that...
It is not that the plan is impossible, but it requires more time.
Not that the plan is impossible, but it requires more time.

rules.zh: （並不是說里奧懶惰，而是他不知道應從哪裏開始。） （里奧停止工作，不是因為懶惰，而是因為他感到不適。）
rules.en: Do not confuse it with not because..., but because... Not that X, but Y corrects an impression or introduces the real point. Not because X, but because Y contrasts two possible reasons for the same action. Compare: Not that Leo is lazy, but he does not know where to begin. Leo stopped working not because he was lazy, but because he felt ill.
examples: Not that X, but Y corrects an impression or introduces the real point.
Not because X, but because Y contrasts two possible reasons for the same action.
Not that Leo is lazy, but he does not know where to begin.

benefits.zh: 這個句型可以幫助你較有禮貌地修正誤解。你不需要直接說對方錯了，而可以先澄清自己並非那 個意思，再說明真正的重點。
benefits.en: It helps you correct a misunderstanding politely Instead of directly telling someone that they are wrong, you can first clarify what you do not mean and then explain your real point.

benefits.zh: 你可以先表示某件事並非完全不好，再指出需要改善的地方，令批評聽起來不會過分直接。 （並不是說你的答案錯了，而是它需要更多支持細節。）
benefits.en: It makes criticism sound less harsh You can acknowledge that something is not completely bad before mentioning the problem. Not that your answer is wrong, but it needs more supporting detail.
examples: You can acknowledge that something is not completely bad before mentioning the problem.
Not that your answer is wrong, but it needs more supporting detail.

benefits.zh: 如果不使用這個句型，你可能需要使用兩句分開的句子，才能完成澄清和解釋。 第二個版本能更流暢地連接兩個意思。
benefits.en: It combines clarification and explanation Without this structure, you may need two separate sentences. Compare: I am not saying that the plan is bad. I am saying that it needs more time. Not that the plan is bad, but it needs more time. The second version connects the two ideas more smoothly.
examples: I am not saying that the plan is bad. I am saying that it needs more time.
Not that the plan is bad, but it needs more time.
The second version connects the two ideas more smoothly.

benefits.zh: 當一件事有優點，但同時存在限制、條件或問題時，這個句型可以幫助你表達較全面和平衡的看 法。
benefits.en: It helps you present a more balanced opinion The structure is useful when something has strengths but also has a limitation, condition or problem.

benefits.zh: 你可以在對話、作文、會議和給予意見時使用這個句型，以澄清立場、回應批評、解釋決定或提出 較婉轉的意見。
benefits.en: It is useful in speaking, essays, meetings and feedback You can use it to clarify your opinion, respond to criticism, explain a decision or give careful feedback.

sourceOmissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules are faithful editorial translations.
